# nonValidEmail

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** an email address.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonValidEmail() — Checks whether a value is **not** an email address. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonValidEmail<T>(value: T | string): value is T;
```

`nonValidEmail(value)` is the same test as `!isValidEmail(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The address is split at a single `@`: the domain is checked the way `isValidDomain` checks one, and the local part must be non-empty and free of spaces. It is a format check, not proof that the mailbox exists.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| string` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not an email address; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonValidEmail("user@@example.com"); // => true
nonValidEmail("user@"); // => true
nonValidEmail("example.com"); // => true
nonValidEmail(""); // => true
nonValidEmail("user@example.com"); // => false
nonValidEmail("first.last@sub.example.co.uk"); // => false
```
